_about: What the SQL parser must find in every dump of the 'shop' database (the source is in src/). Written by hand from the source schemas, NOT from the parser, so it is the oracle of the tests. Names are as stored by each engine (case as written).

weird name.note: a name with a space, and reserved words as column names

postgres.foreignKeys: declared (in ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT for -default, -inserts, -column-inserts and -schema-only)

mysql.dataSyntax: INSERT, several rows per statement (default, -full), one row (-one-row-per-insert), with column names (-complete-insert)

sqlite.dataSyntax: INSERT, one row per statement; the newline is unistr('...\u000a...') in the shell dump and a raw newline in iterdump

duckdb.dataSyntax: COPY ... FROM 'file' (data is in the CSV/Parquet files, not in the SQL)

clickhouse.foreignKeys: none exist in ClickHouse: relationships can only be inferred

awkwardValues: a single quote doubled or escaped: Bob O'Brien
a newline, a semicolon and '--' inside a string: must not end the statement nor start a comment
'/* not a comment */' as a value, and a reserved word used as a column name
a backslash: back\slash path C:\temp (a literal in PostgreSQL and SQLite, an escape in MySQL and ClickHouse)
an emoji and accents (Zoë 😀), NULL, and an empty string
PostgreSQL 17 dumps contain \restrict / \unrestrict meta-commands; MariaDB 11 starts with /*M!999999\- enable the sandbox mode */
